brands.name: Ferrari
brands.headline: Emotion, engineered.
brands.intro: Long bonnets, extraordinary engines and a direct connection to the road. Our Ferrari selection begins with the front-engined V12.

brands.name: Lamborghini
brands.headline: Convention, challenged.
brands.intro: Dramatic proportions meet ambitious engineering. Explore a new chapter for the V12, with electric power joining the combustion engine.

brands.name: Porsche
brands.headline: A line worth following.
brands.intro: A familiar silhouette, constantly reconsidered. Discover the details that turn a road-going 911 into a focused driver’s car.

brands.name: Mercedes-AMG
brands.headline: Performance with presence.
brands.intro: The grand touring tradition, interpreted through AMG. A muscular V8 and a chassis built to make the most of it.

brands.name: BMW
brands.headline: The driver comes first.
brands.intro: Everyday usability meets the technical ambition of M. Look beyond the silhouette to the engines and chassis beneath.

brands.name: Audi
brands.headline: Precision, with a pulse.
brands.intro: Understated forms can hide extraordinary machinery. The R8 puts its naturally aspirated engine at the centre of the experience.

brands.name: McLaren
brands.headline: Every detail earns its place.
brands.intro: Low mass, deliberate aerodynamics and the theatre of a mid-engined supercar. Engineering shapes the experience.

brands.name: Aston Martin
brands.headline: Distance becomes occasion.
brands.intro: British grand touring with a sporting edge. Sculpted bodywork and a driver-focused cabin set the tone for the journey.

brands.name: Bentley
brands.headline: The art of arriving.
brands.intro: A grand tourer balances pace with comfort. Explore the engineering behind Bentley’s W12 interpretation of that idea.

brands.name: Bugatti
brands.headline: An exercise in possibility.
brands.intro: Extraordinary performance calls for equally extraordinary engineering. Discover the original Chiron and its sixteen-cylinder heart.

cars.name: 812 Superfast
cars.power_note: Engine output · 8,500 rpm · includes 5 CV ram effect
cars.intro: A front-mounted V12. A cabin set far back. The 812 Superfast turns classic grand touring proportions into a remarkably focused two-seat berlinetta.
cars.engineering: Its 6.5-litre V12 makes its power without turbocharging. A rear-mounted dual-clutch gearbox and rear-wheel steering help translate that output into a responsive driving experience.
cars.design: The long bonnet and compact tail give the 812 its unmistakable proportions. Inside, the principal controls are arranged around the driver, with a central rev counter giving the engine pride of place.
cars.source_title: Ferrari · 812 Superfast launch and technical specifications
cars.media_gap: Additional exterior, cabin and engine photographs are not yet available for this exact variant.
cars.verification_note: Launch figures checked against Ferrari’s indexed 16 February 2017 release and press PDF. The launch claim is greater than 340 km/h. Power includes the stated 5 CV ram effect. Full webpage requires a JavaScript challenge.

cars.name: Revuelto
cars.engine: 6.5-litre naturally aspirated V12 + three electric motors
cars.intro: The V12 remains the centrepiece. Three electric motors bring a different dimension to Lamborghini’s flagship, pairing a naturally aspirated engine with electrified all-wheel drive.
cars.engineering: The V12 produces 825 PS on its own; the quoted 1,015 PS is the combined system output. A transversely mounted dual-clutch gearbox sits behind the engine.
cars.design: A low wedge, scissor doors and exposed engine form a recognisable Lamborghini composition. The cockpit separates the driver’s instruments, central controls and passenger display.
cars.media_gap: Exterior, cockpit and console photographs are included. An exact-variant engine photograph is still unavailable.
cars.verification_note: Checked against Lamborghini’s model specifications and digital brochure. Power is combined system output; torque is V12 output only. The 2023 launch date is supported by manufacturer news; brochure accessible through indexed text.

cars.name: 911 GT3
cars.intro: A familiar outline with a distinctly motorsport purpose. This 992.1 GT3 pairs the naturally aspirated flat-six with PDK and the standard fixed rear wing.
cars.engineering: Double-wishbone front suspension and a swan-neck-mounted rear wing connect the GT3 to Porsche’s racing work. These figures are for PDK; the six-speed manual has different acceleration and top-speed figures.
cars.design: The fixed wing and front airflow openings make function visible. The cabin keeps the driving instruments close at hand, with a track display that prioritises the essentials.
cars.media_gap: Exterior and wheel-detail photographs are included. Cabin and engine photographs are still unavailable; the photographed transmission has not been independently established.
cars.verification_note: Checked against 2021 Porsche Newsroom and the February 2021 PDK technical sheet. Values apply to 992.1 PDK, not manual, Touring-specific equipment or the later 992.2. PDF extraction was limited; indexed technical text was available.

cars.name: AMG GT 63
cars.intro: The second-generation AMG GT brings all-wheel drive to the two-door coupé. Its long bonnet houses a twin-turbo V8, with a wider brief that includes long-distance comfort.
cars.engineering: The 63’s V8 drives through a nine-speed transmission and fully variable all-wheel drive. Active roll stabilisation and rear-axle steering help manage the car’s responses.
cars.design: A broad grille and fastback roof define the exterior. The portrait-oriented central display sits within a cabin that brings the controls towards the driver.
cars.source_title: Mercedes-Benz Media · 2023 AMG GT Coupé launch
cars.media_gap: Exact-variant photography is unavailable in this local edition. No substitute car image has been used.
cars.verification_note: Checked against the indexed 19 August 2023 German launch release and technical table for the two-door GT 63 4MATIC+. Torque RPM is omitted because the source prose and table disagree about the upper RPM limit.

cars.name: M4 Competition
cars.intro: The G82 M4 Competition combines a straight-six engine with a usable four-seat coupé. This record covers the original rear-wheel-drive version, before later xDrive and power updates.
cars.engineering: Two turbochargers feed the six-cylinder engine. An eight-speed automatic transmission sends power to the rear wheels. The listed top speed is the standard electronic limit.
cars.design: A pronounced grille and wide wheel arches distinguish the M4. The cockpit brings configurable driving settings together with clearly arranged instruments and supportive seats.
cars.source_title: BMW PressClub · 2021 M4 Competition UK launch
cars.media_gap: Exact-variant photography is unavailable in this local edition. No substitute car image has been used.
cars.verification_note: Checked against the readable 9 March 2021 UK launch release and BMW’s 2021 technical tables. Rear-wheel-drive Competition specification, with the standard 250 km/h electronic limiter; optional higher limit excluded.

cars.name: R8 V10 performance
cars.intro: A mid-mounted V10 and quattro traction give the R8 its distinctive combination of drama and composure. This is the facelift performance coupé, rather than the Spyder or rear-drive version.
cars.engineering: The aluminium and carbon-fibre structure surrounds a naturally aspirated V10. A seven-speed dual-clutch gearbox delivers power to the quattro drivetrain.
cars.design: The side blades frame the engine bay and air intakes. A driver-centred digital instrument display keeps the cabin focused, with no separate centre infotainment screen.
cars.media_gap: Exact-variant photography is unavailable in this local edition. No substitute car image has been used.
cars.verification_note: Checked against Audi’s June 2019 facts, engine and transmission pages and indexed 2019 technical material. These are facelift performance quattro coupé figures; later engine RPM updates and RWD/Spyder variants are excluded.

cars.name: 750S
cars.intro: McLaren’s 750S builds its character around low mass and a carbon-fibre structure. The coupé keeps the twin-turbo V8 behind the cabin and sends its output to the rear wheels.
cars.engineering: The 750S combines a seven-speed gearbox with linked hydraulic suspension. Its focus is response: to steering inputs, throttle changes and the surface beneath the tyres.
cars.design: Dihedral doors open into a compact cockpit. Slim pillars support outward visibility, while an active rear wing gives the clean bodywork a functional finishing point.
cars.media_gap: Additional exterior, cabin and engine photographs are not yet available for this exact variant.
cars.verification_note: Checked against indexed McLaren model specifications. 750 PS is metric horsepower; manufacturer listings also report 552 kW and 3,994 cm³. Current page extraction is limited; indexed specification text supplies performance and seven-speed SSG details.

cars.name: DB12
cars.intro: Aston Martin’s DB12 gives the grand tourer a sharper sporting brief. The original coupé combines V8 power with a redesigned cabin; this record does not cover the later DB12 S.
cars.engineering: A twin-turbo V8 feeds a rear-mounted eight-speed transmission. An electronic rear differential and adaptive dampers help balance traction, control and touring comfort.
cars.design: Broad shoulders and a low roofline frame the traditional front-engined proportions. The centre console combines a touchscreen with physical controls for frequently used functions.
cars.media_gap: Exact-variant photography is unavailable in this local edition. No substitute car image has been used.
cars.verification_note: Launch year, engine, output, torque RPM, acceleration, speed and transmission checked against Aston Martin’s 2023 release and readable DB12 model page. Exact cubic-centimetre displacement: Not verified in accessible primary material.

cars.name: Continental GT Speed
cars.intro: The W12-powered third-generation GT Speed brings a more focused chassis to Bentley’s grand tourer. This is the 2021 coupé, not the later hybrid generation or convertible.
cars.engineering: The W12 pairs substantial torque with all-wheel drive. Electronic all-wheel steering and an electronic limited-slip differential sharpen its responses.
cars.design: A long bonnet, muscular rear haunches and a compact glasshouse set the proportions. Inside, traditional materials sit alongside the technology expected of a long-distance car.
cars.media_gap: Exact-variant photography is unavailable in this local edition. No substitute car image has been used.
cars.verification_note: Checked against Bentley’s indexed 23 March 2021 coupé launch release: W12, 659 PS, 900 Nm, 3.6 seconds, 335 km/h and eight-speed dual-clutch transmission. Exact cubic-centimetre displacement: Not verified in accessible primary material.

cars.name: Chiron
cars.intro: The original Chiron brought a sixteen-cylinder engine into a carefully composed grand touring form. Its immense output is supported by a drivetrain and cooling system designed around the same ambition.
cars.engineering: Four turbochargers feed the W16, with power delivered through a seven-speed dual-clutch gearbox and all-wheel drive. The quoted maximum speed is electronically limited for road use.
cars.design: The sweeping side curve connects the cabin to the rear bodywork. Inside, a narrow centre stack and clear instruments contrast with the technical complexity beneath.
cars.media_gap: Additional exterior, cabin and engine photographs are not yet available for this exact variant.
cars.verification_note: Original model and drivetrain checked against Bugatti’s readable 29 February 2016 launch release. Exact cubic-centimetre displacement and original launch acceleration claim: Not verified. A later manufacturer retrospective reports 2.4 seconds, not a contemporaneous launch figure.
